directions: WARNING: ALL PARTS OF THIS PLANT ARE HIGHLY TOXIC IF INGESTED — keep it away from grazing animals and small children, and never burn the trimmings. Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. 'Petite Salmon' holds to a compact 3 to 6 foot mound and carries single, warm salmon-pink flowers in loose clusters from late spring through fall, giving it a softer, warmer tone than the cooler pink of 'Petite Pink'. Its small stature suits foundation beds, median strips, and large containers where a standard oleander would quickly outgrow the space, and it shares the species' ease with heat, drought, and salt spray once rooted in.

Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. Named for Magnolia Willis Sealy of Galveston, Texas, this long-grown Gulf Coast selection bears soft, clear pink single flowers in open clusters from late spring through fall on an upright shrub that reaches 6 to 8 feet. It is a traditional choice for a tall informal hedge or windbreak along the coast, tolerating salt spray, heat, and drought with the same indifference as the rest of the species.

Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. 'Casablanca' produces large, single white flowers, sometimes faintly flushed pink in the throat, over a long season from summer into fall on a vigorous shrub that reaches 8 to 10 feet tall and wide. Its size and dense habit make it well suited to a tall privacy screen or background planting, and like other oleanders it tolerates heat, drought, salt spray, and poor soil once established.

Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. 'Algiers' is a free-blooming, deep dark red single-flowered oleander that forms a dense, mounding shrub 5 to 8 feet tall, and it is sometimes limbed up and trained into a small multi-trunk standard for use as a patio or street tree. Flowers appear in clusters from late spring through fall, and the plant shares the species' tolerance for heat, drought, salt spray, and lean soil.

directions: WARNING: ALL PARTS OF THIS PLANT ARE HIGHLY TOXIC IF INGESTED — keep it out of reach of grazing animals and small children, and never burn the prunings. Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. 'Pink Beauty' is a tall, vigorous grower bearing large, clear pink single flowers in loose terminal clusters from late spring through fall, and it tolerates light frost somewhat better than many other pink oleanders. Left untrimmed it builds into a substantial background shrub or small multi-trunk tree, making it well suited to a tall screen or windbreak, and it carries the species' usual indifference to heat, drought, and salt spray once established.

directions: WARNING: ALL PARTS OF THIS PLANT ARE HIGHLY TOXIC IF INGESTED — keep it away from grazing animals and small children, and never burn the trimmings. Root semi-hardwood cuttings in spring or set out container plants once the soil has warmed, in ordinary well-drained soil in full sun. 'Little Red' stays compact at 3 to 6 feet tall and wide, carrying deep red single flowers over a long summer-into-fall bloom season on a naturally dense, rounded frame that needs little shaping. Its small size suits foundation plantings, low informal hedges, and large containers where a full-size red oleander would be out of scale, and it is just as heat-, drought-, and salt-tolerant as its larger relatives.
